author: .just_kk
content:
if we want to let anyone (not only proposer) to participate in final aggregation I believe it makes sense to introduce a new topic for global aggregates (proving all committees for the slot). Drafted a PR here.

Open questions is what kind of validation rules we should have for this topic. I.e. should we propagate any global aggregate, or only the ones that prove more attester signatures than the previous best (maybe by some margin).

Happy to hear any thoughts

https://github.com/jtraglia/consensus-specs/pull/14

author: barnabemonnot
content: Is there a big difference in DOS-resistance/good properties if we had some sampled redundant global aggregators instead?

author: yannvonlanthen
content: Similar to Barnabé's question, but the other way around: what property does this give us? Is the idea of this proposal that a proposer could get the final aggregate from this topic? I assume that this would move all deadlines up by 1-2 seconds?

author: .just_kk
content:
this would simplify dos protection, yes. But sampling should be designed in a way to ensure that every slot we have someone producing the global proof.
Or we can simply allow only validators with stake above some threshold to produce such proofs (just throwing as idea)

author: .just_kk
content:
this is to further derisk scenario when proposer has weak hardware and cannot aggregate in time. I believe this is the direction we are going anyway (not forcing proposer to be proof producer). 

If there is no proof from the network proposer would have to produce it himself

author: barnabemonnot
content:
we should have numbers on this, but basically there are three modes:
- proposer only produces aggregate
- proposer + sampled aggregators produce redundant aggregates
- anyone can propose aggregates

we want high QoS without exposing ourselves to too much overhead from redundant aggregates + be protected from DoS. I'd be surprised if sampling O(10) aggregators per slot isn't enough to have pretty high QoS

author: .just_kk
content:
ideally these global aggregators would have to be subscribed to all attestation subnets (so they don't need to wait for subnet proofs, but can perform both signature and recursive aggregation themselves).

Therefore I don't want to have the assumption where some validator is **forced** to be such global aggregator as this would be too much overhead for home stakers. 

If instead we could let validators to volunteer to become global validators and then sample only among them that would be the best scenario

author: barnabemonnot
content:
right, we can raise sample quality with self-selection perhaps, but we might also crowd out people who are able to do the job but wouldn't default in because it's opt-in. doesn't seem bad to me if the sample size is high but we expect some share of global aggregators to not do the job.

tl;dr maybe better to let people opt-out than having them opt-in

author: barnabemonnot
content: at the same time if it's "free" to also just have a permissionless topic, why not. could have that as a complement to a sampled set of aggregators too

author: kevaundray
content: When you say aggregates, can you clarify if you mean the global aggregate or the subnet aggregates?

author: barnabemonnot
content: I mean the global aggregate here

author: kevaundray
content:
> anyone can propose aggregates

Also trying to understand: here do you mean that anyone can produce an aggregate, that the proposer will then include in their block if they see it on the global topic?

author: .just_kk
content: this might work. We have operators having thousands of validators. I think it is fair to assume that they will be sampled almost every slot as global proof producers

author: barnabemonnot
content: yes, but I believe this is what Kamil's EIP suggests. i was suggesting the middle path of sampling a few redundant global aggregators

author: kevaundray
content: Can't we reuse the subnet aggregators for the global topic?

author: .just_kk
content: (for the record there is no EIP yet, this new topic could be a new EIP or be part of general PQ EIP)

author: barnabemonnot
content: that could be interesting, e.g., big operators would have been sampled across multiple topics likely, so they possibly already have the subnet aggregates in hand to make a global one with them

author: kevaundray
content: Do we also allow builders to be aggregators?

author: barnabemonnot
content:
right that could be a fourth option
1. proposer only
2. proposer + sampled validators
3. proposer + sampled validators + builders
4. anyone

author: barnabemonnot
content: idk how different 3 and 4 are really. registering as builder is pretty permissionless, so if my goal as an attacker is to DoS the topic, I could easily Sybil the builder registry I suppose

author: .just_kk
content:
TLDR: Yes, we can. It is very likely that there are super high-stake nodes among these aggregators. 

Assuming that only that nodes with high stake are capable of performing global aggregation, we will have at least one such node in every slot. 

Also confirmed this with Claude. Even if we assume that only the node sampled as a subnet aggregator and possessing at least 200k ETH in stake is capable of performing global aggregation, in 99% of the time we will still have at least one such node

author: yannvonlanthen
content: Just to make sure, do I understand correctly that we are talking PQ-Gasper here, and that adding global aggregators means that now there is an additional delay for global aggregate propagation on the critical path? (which IIRC that was not there when discussing PQ-Gasper in Mumbai)

author: terencechain
content:
Not directly related to networking, potentially a good add-on, when the proposer requests a bid, the builder could also return its best set of attestations and its proof. The proposer verifies them and uses them if they’re compatible and better than what it has locally
I’m not worried about DoS here since it’s direct RPC. Verification and replacement should be cheap as well. We’d still want response size limits and a timeout and local aggregate as fallback

author: yannvonlanthen
content: Totally agree, I proposed the same thing a few weeks back. It also makes economic sense, since aggregations give rewards, so you could even bundle them in with your bid (though I recognize that that's more controversial)

author: .just_kk
content:
it could be applied to both PQ gasper and PQ DC I suppose.

what do you mean by additional delay? if it is time to create the global aggregation, yes it is on a critical path. But it is expected to be performed by some sophisticated entities that can do such aggregation relatively quickly

author: tcoratger
content:
We must be careful about sampling or similar methods on the aggregator that we pick at the end. 

Indeed, the recursion step in the VM is a bit demanding for the CPU. Going to the extreme if while sampling, we come across a node that has a 15 year old laptop, we can potentially break things by waiting way to much for the aggregate to arrive! 

You still need a minimum amount of hardware to aggregate in a reasonable amount of time, no GPU or stuffs like this but a decent computer. Typically the benchmarks from the leanVM repo were made on M4 Max Macbook.

author: .just_kk
content: The same thing could happen to proposer if it slow and should aggregate himself. Which is why global proof topic / proof request to builder should be there to derisk not having proof on time
